tasks.title: file-tidy: harden Linux trash for byte names, other mounts and relative XDG_DATA_HOME
tasks.prompt:
file-tidy's Linux (freedesktop) trash support in `skills/file-tidy/scripts/file_tidy.py` has three bugs.

1. `write_trashinfo(dest, original)` breaks on file names that are not valid UTF-8 (e.g. a POSIX name containing byte 0xE9). The `Path=` line must percent-encode the raw file-name bytes, keeping `/` unescaped: for original `os.fsdecode(b"/srv/caf\xe9 1.txt")` the file must contain `Path=/srv/caf%E9%201.txt`.

2. `trash_dir()` honours a relative `XDG_DATA_HOME`. The XDG spec says a relative value must be ignored; on Linux with `XDG_DATA_HOME=relative/share` it must return `~/.local/share/Trash/files`.

3. Trashing an item that lives on another mount (e.g. a USB drive) silently copies it into the home trash. Add a module-level function `on_trash_volume(src: Path) -> bool` that reports whether `src` is on the same device as the home trash (use the nearest existing ancestor if the trash folder does not exist yet). When planning an apply (`apply <plan> --apply`), a `trash` item on a freedesktop system (`freedesktop_trash()` true) whose source is not on the trash volume must abort with `SystemExit` whose message contains `use move instead`, before anything moves.

Tests run with `python3 -m unittest discover -s skills/file-tidy/scripts -p 'test_*.py'`; add tests for each case. Nice to have: mention in the Undo section of `skills/file-tidy/SKILL.md` that trash refuses items on another mount.
tasks.parts: One module: file_tidy.py plus its test file; the SKILL.md line is a one-sentence doc touch, not worth a separate worker.

tasks.title: worktree-tidy: keep ignored secrets and unpushed branch commits
tasks.prompt:
`skills/worktree-tidy/scripts/worktree_tidy.py` can lose work: `git worktree remove` silently deletes ignored files (e.g. `.env`), and `--delete-branch` runs `branch -D` after a merged request even if local commits were added later.

Required:
- `dirty_paths(path)` makes exactly one `git --no-optional-locks status ... --ignored=matching` call and returns `(dirty, ignored)` or None. Ignored paths are fine when regenerable: any segment in module set `REGENERABLE_DIRS` (node_modules, build, generated, ... and similar), a prefix in `REGENERABLE_PREFIXES` (`.husky/_/`), or `*.log`. Secrets (`.env`, `.env.*`, `id_rsa*`, `*.pem`, `*.key`, ...) are never regenerable, even inside collapsed build/generated folders (walk them, but not node_modules). Other ignored paths add Blocker `ignored`. Scan uses at most 6 subprocess calls per worktree.
- `add_regenerable(list)` extends those sets (entries with `/` are prefixes); non-list raises SystemExit; config key `regenerable`.
- Each row adds `shortHead`, `subject`, `dirtyFiles` (max 10, rename targets included), `ignored` (count), `ignoredFiles` (max 10), `branchSaved` (branch commits all on another branch/tag/remote ref), `unpushed` (HEAD commits on no remote ref; null without remote refs). Missing folders: empty/0/False/None.
- `branchDeletable` and dry-run `wouldDeleteBranch` also require `branchSaved`.
- `remove(paths, days, delete_branch, use_orca, yes, allow_recent=False)` and CLI `--allow-recent`: allow removal when blockers are exactly `["recent"]`.
- Right before removing, re-check status; on change error `not removable: changed since it was checked`. Before deleting a branch re-check it; if unsaved keep it with `branchError` `branch has commits that exist on no other ref; kept`.

Document these in SKILL.md (nice-to-have).
tasks.parts: Mostly one module (worktree_tidy.py); SKILL.md and references/glossary.md docs can go to a second worker, but the code changes in dirty_paths/assess/remove are interdependent and should not be split.

tasks.title: validate-skills: enforce the 1024-character, tag-free description and fit figma-mcp in it
tasks.prompt:
`scripts/validate-skills.mjs` only checks that a skill `description` is at least 20 characters. The Agent Skills spec also requires at most 1024 characters and no XML tags, and `skills/figma-mcp/SKILL.md` currently violates both (it is over 1024 characters and contains `<url>`).

Required:
- Export `DESCRIPTION_MAX_LENGTH` (1024) and `descriptionProblems(rawDescription)` from `scripts/validate-skills.mjs`. It trims the input, counts characters (not bytes), and returns an array of problem strings (empty when fine). Keep the existing too-short message (contains `过短`). For an over-long description the message must include the actual length as `<n> 字符` (e.g. `1025 字符`) and the fix hint `删掉重复的触发词`. For XML-like tags the message must list the tags found (e.g. `<url>`); plain comparisons such as `count < 30 and > 5` are not tags.
- `main()` must report each problem per skill, and importing the module must not run validation (only run `main()` when the file is executed directly).
- Shorten the `skills/figma-mcp/SKILL.md` description to at most 1024 characters with no angle-bracket tags, keeping its meaning; bump its `metadata.version` patch.
- `pnpm skills:validate` must pass.

Nice to have: add `./scripts/__tests__/validate-skills.test.mjs` to the root `test:scripts` script and regenerate the skills index with `pnpm skills:index`.
tasks.parts: Two independent file sets: scripts/validate-skills.mjs (+ package.json test:scripts) and skills/figma-mcp/SKILL.md description rewrite; they only meet at the final pnpm skills:validate.
